siteSafety.check: Website safety check (/safe, basic tier: passive signals only, no blocklist), false-alarm test
siteSafety.data: 398 popular sites (ranks 300 to 300,000 of a public top-1M list, assumed legitimate; some are piracy or adult sites, so a few flags may be fair)

phishingListed.note: No phishing detection rate is published. An earlier test of the basic /safe check against a public list of 'active' phishing links was withdrawn: nearly all of the pages that answered were already taken down (Cloudflare 'Suspected Phishing' warnings, 404s, parked or deleted sites). A second try with a fresher feed found only about 6 live phishing pages out of 172 listed, far too few to measure a rate. So treat the basic /safe check as a technical-signals check (HTTPS, headers, redirects, forms, domain age), not a phishing detector. The paid /safe-pro tier adds a Google Web Risk lookup, which this test does not cover.

siteSafety.note: Sites that could not be reached are left out of the rates. A dead phishing site is not a detection. The paid /safe-pro tier adds a Google Web Risk lookup, which this test does not cover.

caveats: Samples are small, so each rate comes with a 95% interval. A wide interval means the true rate could be well above or below the figure.
The popular-site set leans toward sites with decent security settings, so false-alarm rates are probably lower than on the wider web.
Listed phishing domains include hacked legitimate sites and parked or dead pages; dead ones are excluded, and a flagged result is not proof a site is phishing.
These results come from running the check code on a desktop computer. The live service runs on Cloudflare Workers, which can differ slightly (for example, reading certificate details).
Honeypot, preflight and sanctions checks are not covered yet.
